summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with worsening dyspnea, bilateral lower extremity edema, and urinary incontinence, following non-adherence to Lasix and a recent UTI. Evaluation revealed volume overload due to acute on chronic diastolic heart failure, with no evidence of pulmonary embolism on V/Q scan. A urine culture grew ESBL-producing E. coli, treated with oral Bactrim. She responded well to IV and oral furosemide, with improved symptoms and weight reduction. Her subtherapeutic INR was corrected with warfarin adjustment. She was discharged on oral diuretics, anticoagulation, and antibiotics, with home oxygen, a bariatric bed, and home nursing support arranged for follow-up care.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Chronic hepatitis C without mention of hepatic coma
Asymptomatic human immunodeficiency virus [HIV] infection status
Escherichia coli [E. coli] infection in conditions classified elsewhere and of unspecified site
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
